exercise_records.title: Absolute and relative sensitivity.
exercise_records.prompt: Let \(f(x)=3x^2+2\). Find \(f'(4)\) and the local relative sensitivity \(xf'(x)/f(x)\) at \(x=4\).
exercise_records.solution: \(f'(x)=6x\), so \(f'(4)=24\). Since \(f(4)=50\), the elasticity is \(4(24)/50=1.92\). A 1% local change in \(x\) corresponds to approximately 1.92% change in \(f\).
exercise_records.review: Derivative24/elasticity96/50=1.92 analytically correct;matching generic-helper execution remainspending.

exercise_records.title: Exponential elasticity.
exercise_records.prompt: For \(f(x)=e^{2x}\), derive \(xf'(x)/f(x)\) and evaluate at \(x=0.5\).
exercise_records.solution: \(f'=2e^{2x}\), so elasticity is \(2x\); at \(x=0.5\), it equals 1.
exercise_records.review: Elasticity2x=1 at.5;analytic review,not a newfunction execution here.

exercise_records.title: When relative sensitivity fails.
exercise_records.prompt: Explain why \(f'(x)/f(x)\) is undefined when \(f(x)=0\). Give a financial reporting alternative.
exercise_records.solution: The denominator vanishes. Report absolute sensitivity and scenario changes in currency units, or normalize by a documented nonzero reference scale rather than silently dividing by zero.

exercise_records.title: Ten-basis-point scenario.
exercise_records.prompt: For Exercise 9, find the linear and quadratic value changes for \(h=+0.001\).
exercise_records.solution: \(\Delta V_1=-5V(0.001)\approx-40.936538\). The quadratic correction is \(25V(0.001)^2/2\approx0.102341\), so \(\Delta V_2\approx-40.834196\).

exercise_records.title: Exact scenario and error.
exercise_records.prompt: For Exercise 11, write the exact change and the signed quadratic error.
exercise_records.solution: \(\Delta V_{\rm exact}=V\operatorname{expm1}(-0.005)\). The signed error is \(E_2=V[\operatorname{expm1}(-0.005)+0.005-0.005^2/2]\), which is negative. Its magnitude is approximately \(0.000170356\).

exercise_records.prompt: Bound the error in Exercise 12.

exercise_records.title: Duration/convexity inequality.
exercise_records.prompt: Prove \(K\ge D^2\) for positive fixed cash flows.
exercise_records.solution: Let \(w_i=C_ie^{-rt_i}/V\), so \(w_i>0\) and \(\sum_iw_i=1\). Then \(K-D^2=\sum_iw_i(t_i-D)^2\ge0\).

exercise_records.title: Cash-flow sensitivity.
exercise_records.prompt: Find \(\partial V/\partial C_i\) for a fixed payment \(C_i\) at \(t_i\).
exercise_records.solution: \(\partial V/\partial C_i=e^{-rt_i}\). The elasticity of \(V\) with respect to \(C_i\) is \(C_ie^{-rt_i}/V\).

exercise_records.title: Call payoff.
exercise_records.prompt: Let \(g(S)=\max(S-100,0)\). Find its left and right derivatives at \(S=100\).
exercise_records.solution: Left slope 0; right slope 1. There is no two-sided derivative.

exercise_records.title: Centered difference trap.
exercise_records.prompt: Calculate \([g(102)-g(98)]/4\) for Exercise 17. Explain why the result is misleading.
exercise_records.solution: \((2-0)/4=0.5\), although the true one-sided slopes are 0 and 1. The centered quotient is not the derivative at the kink.

exercise_records.title: Cap and floor.
exercise_records.prompt: For \(f(r)=1000\min(\max(r,0.02),0.05)\), state the one-sided derivatives at \(r=0.02\) and \(r=0.05\).
exercise_records.solution: At the floor: left 0, right 1000. At the cap: left 1000, right 0.

exercise_records.title: Offset of kinks.
exercise_records.prompt: Show \(\max(S-K,0)-\max(K-S,0)=S-K\).
exercise_records.solution: For \(S\ge K\), the difference is \((S-K)-0\); for \(S<K\), it is \(0-(K-S)\). Thus the combined payoff is smooth despite nonsmooth components.

exercise_records.title: Nonparallel shocks.
exercise_records.prompt: For independent spot rates \(z_i\) and shocks \(h_i\), derive a first-order value change.
exercise_records.solution: \(\Delta V_1=-\sum_i t_iC_ie^{-z_it_i}h_i\). This is a cash-flow-level spot-rate sensitivity, not necessarily a market key-rate duration.

exercise_records.title: Error denominator.
exercise_records.prompt: Why is \(|E_2|/|\Delta V_{\rm exact}|\) unreliable near a zero exact change?
exercise_records.solution: It is undefined at zero and numerically unstable for tiny exact changes. Report absolute currency error and, if appropriate, error relative to a nonzero baseline value.

exercise_records.title: Acceptance decision.
exercise_records.prompt: A report passes all mathematical remainder checks but uses an unverified cash-flow schedule. Can it be called production-certified?
exercise_records.solution: No. A remainder bound verifies an approximation within the specified mathematical model. It does not validate source cash flows, curve calibration, financial assumptions, runtime evidence, or independent review.
